_comment: Mechanical encoding of products/around-the-world-80-days/day-01-london/scenes/README.md, section 'Linear cut', into render hints.
script: ordered tokens — s:N / s:N-M = narration sentence(s) by index (0-based, splitter in render_linear.mjs; the numbered list is in linear/render-log.md),
quiz:correct = correct option text + its feedback, chat:N = chip N question + answer (answer in voice2), overlay:N = the overlay text, game:list = the correct drag options.
No words are invented here: every token points at text that already exists in the scene JSON. Where the README seconds are shorter than the TTS,
render_linear.mjs end-cuts at a sentence boundary and logs it — the Narrator owns the final trim.
visuals: kind image|clip|player|scenecard|pending|quiz|chat|checklist|streetview; dur in seconds or omitted = share the remainder.
overlays: indices into scene.overlays, or {i, at, until} to re-time for the shorter linear scene. beds: {media, at, until}.

A4 2026-08-19: all sentence tokens re-derived after the A3n newcomer rewrite (old indices were stale and cut payoffs: Sheridan reveal, the route legs, the carpet-bag beat, the forgotten gas, the recipe). Linear cut is now ~13 min, longer than the original 11:42 plan, deliberately: coherence beats the target length.

A5 2026-08-19 (Narrator): the A4 tokens were derived from the STANDARD track but the film renders the CLEAR one (`--track clear`), whose sentences split differently (192 vs 181) — that mismatch is what produced the dangling references in review/fact-check-a5.md §4. Every `s:N` below is now re-derived against `narration.variants.clear` (`node render_linear.mjs <tour.json> --plan --track clear`) on three rules: keep the narrative spine; never leave a reference without its antecedent (Henry Poole is named before 'The firm says…', the club before 'It is real…', the carpet-bag before the packing list, the recipe card before it is mentioned); drop interactive-only instructions ('Tap any line', 'Drag in what goes', 'Save the card.', 'Now tap the longest leg', 'Ask him something', 'Take your time'). Re-derive after ANY script edit: the indices are per-track and per-wording.
